name: Jezero Crater · Three Forks Sample Depot
region: Jezero crater floor and the western delta front
scene: Jezero crater's floor and the edge of its delta
story: Two astronauts walk out from the habitat on the floor of Jezero crater to Three Forks, where Perseverance laid ten sealed sample tubes on the ground in 2022-23 as a backup cache for Mars Sample Return. They recover two tubes, climb the delta front to Wildcat Ridge, the lake mudstone behind Perseverance's most promising organic-bearing samples, look at the Amalik outcrop, and walk home before their consumables or daylight run low.
frame_note: Coordinates are on the USGS DTM. The stops come from Mars 2020 team maps (sample sites, the depot), so they were moved by the measured team-frame shift (-22.6 m east, +20.7 m north): data-use item D6.

crism_notes.HYD: Red = polyhydrated sulfates, green = monohydrated sulfates, blue = bound water. Hydrated minerals mark where water once soaked the delta and the lake-floor rocks; Perseverance found sulfate-bearing sandstone at the base of the delta front.
crism_notes.PHY: Red = Fe/Mg clays, green = Al clays, blue = bound water. CRISM's Fe/Mg-clay and carbonate signatures in the delta are why Jezero was chosen: clays settle out in still lake water and can preserve organic matter.
crism_notes.MAF: Red = olivine, green = low-calcium pyroxene, blue = high-calcium pyroxene. The crater floor (Séítah and Máaz) is olivine- and pyroxene-rich igneous rock, and dark basaltic sand drifts between the outcrops.
crism_notes.FEM: Iron-bearing minerals: red = crystalline ferric oxides, green and blue = other ferric and ferrous absorptions. Olivine-rich floor rocks show strong ferrous bands; altered delta layers lean ferric.

stops.name: Three Forks Depot
tasks: Match each tube on the ground to the depot map
Photograph two tubes in place, then pick them up
Stow both tubes in the sealed sample caddy
Leave a radio beacon marking the remaining tubes
stops.science: Perseverance laid ten sealed tubes on the crater floor here between December 2022 and January 2023, a backup cache for Mars Sample Return holding cores of delta and crater-floor rock, regolith and atmosphere.

stops.name: Wildcat Ridge
tasks: Hammer sample of the finely layered mudstone
Close-up imaging of the bedding planes
Find Perseverance's abrasion patch for comparison
stops.science: Fine-grained mudstone laid down in the lake about 3.5 billion years ago. Perseverance's SHERLOC instrument found organic-molecule signals here, and the rover cored it twice (Hazeltop and Bearwallow, July-August 2022).

stops.name: Amalik Outcrop
stops.science: Sulfate-bearing sandstones and mudstones near the base of the delta front, cored by Perseverance as Shuyak and Mageik in October 2022.

shelters.name: Pressurized rover PR-2
shelters.note: Parked between the hab and the depot. Pressurized cabin with a water-wall storm shelter.

lake.source: Mangold et al., Past variations of water level of Jezero paleolake, LPSC 2024 (NTRS 20240000546)
lake.note: Delta-front beds record Jezero's lake falling from about -2,410 m (fan top, north of Belva crater) to -2,500 m (Kodiak, Eastern Cape) as it dried in a closed basin below the eastern breach (about -2,400 m). The whole Three Forks site lies below the breach: the mudstones the samples come from were laid down under this water.

levels.name: Eastern breach (the lake at its outlet)
